context: On the anniversary of Hiroshi-elder's death. Three women — wife, two daughters — sit together for tea.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 今日は、お父さんの命日ね。皆、来てくれて、ありがとう。
lines.en: Today is your father's memorial day. Thank you all for coming.
lines.style: Soft opening, voice warm with decades of grief held gently. Speaking to the room as its center. Grateful underneath the steadiness. A pause after 'day' — she's steadying herself.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: お母さん、毎年、こうやって、皆で集まれて、嬉しい。
lines.en: Mother, I'm so glad we can gather like this every year.
lines.style: Warm and direct, the way a daughter speaks to her mother when they both know what's being said. Sincere without sentimentality. Steady presence in the voice.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 私も。お父さん、絶対、見てくれてる。
lines.en: Me too. He's definitely watching over us.
lines.style: Quick, certain, leaning forward slightly in the voice. Not performative — conviction. A small nod at the end of the thought, audible in the breath.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: もう、何年経っても、寂しさは、変わらないけど。
lines.en: But no matter how many years pass, the loneliness doesn't change.
lines.style: Quiet honesty. No fight in it. The voice thins slightly on 'doesn't change' — she's said this before, knows it will remain true. Accepting without resignation.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: お父さんとの思い出、心の中で、ずっと、生きてるから。
lines.en: Because the memories we have with him — they live on in our hearts.
lines.style: Gentle, almost meditative. Lifting slightly on 'memories,' settling on 'hearts.' Speaking something she believes completely. Slow enough to let it land.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: お父さん、メイちゃんの結婚式も、見てくれた。指輪、ずっと、メイがしてる。
lines.en: He saw Mei's wedding too. She still wears the ring he gave her.
lines.style: Reflective, almost marveling. A small smile in the voice. The mention of the ring carries weight — tangible proof of his presence continuing. Warm nostalgia.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 形見が、こうやって、繋がっていくの、本当に、嬉しいわね。
lines.en: It makes me so happy when his keepsakes connect us like this.
lines.style: Voice softens on 'keepsakes.' There's wonder here — the miracle of continuity. Not wistful, but genuinely pleased. A small lift at the end, like she's sharing something precious.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 孫たちも、よく、おじいちゃんの話、するんですよ。
lines.en: The grandchildren talk about their grandfather quite often, you know.
lines.style: Brightening slightly. Proud, almost delighted. A hint of 'see how he lives on through them' underneath. Warm observation, the way she shares good news about family.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お父さん、絶対、嬉しいわ。
lines.en: He must be so happy about that.
lines.style: Certain and tender. Not a question — a quiet affirmation. Voice carries the fullness of faith without needing to defend it. Soft close on the word 'happy.'

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: 私たち、家族、ずっと、繋がっていけたらいいな。
lines.en: I hope our family can stay connected like this forever.
lines.style: Reaching forward in the voice. Not demanding — wishing. A certain vulnerability here, the deepest longing of the evening. Quiet, sincere, almost a prayer.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: お父さん、ありがとう。ずっと、私たち、見てくれてる。
lines.en: Thank you, father. You're always watching over us.
lines.style: Direct address, intimate and reverent at once. Voice steady and full at the same time. Gratitude and faith spoken as one thing. Closing address to him, not to the room.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 皆で、お線香、上げましょうか。
lines.style: Gentle turn toward ritual. A question that's also an invitation. Voice settles into the ceremony. Leading without commanding. Warm and certain.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: うん、お父さんと、お話、しよう。
lines.en: Yes, let's talk to him together.
lines.style: Quick agreement, immediate. Warmth and readiness. Matching the grandmother's movement toward ritual. The voice carries the easiness of doing this together, year after year.
